t: #3568 Minimum Moves to Clean the Classroom — State-Space BFS
o: We must collect up to 10 litter items while managing an energy budget that only refills on 'R' cells, minimizing total moves. Since moves cost 1 uniformly, BFS over an expanded state space gives shortest answers. The state must capture position, which litter is collected (bitmask, ≤2^10), and remaining energy (≤50) — about 20·20·1024·51 ≈ 20M states worst case, feasible. Example 2 shows why energy alone is insufficient: after picking the first 'L' we detour to 'R' to refill before the second. Obstacles 'X' simply block expansion.
k: Encode litter collection as a bitmask — with ≤10 litter cells, 1024 masks are affordable.
Energy must be part of the BFS state because reaching a cell with 0 energy (not on 'R') is a dead end, while the same cell with energy is not.
Uniform move cost ⇒ plain level-by-level BFS yields the minimum move count.

a.n: Approach 1: BFS over (position, litter mask, energy)
a.i: Run BFS where each node is (row, col, mask, energy). Moving costs 1 energy; stepping on 'R' restores energy to full, stepping on 'L' sets its mask bit. The first time we pop a state with the full mask, the BFS level is the answer.
s: Precompute litter ids and the full mask.
BFS level by level; skip 'X' cells and moves made with 0 energy.
On 'R' reset energy to max; on 'L' set the corresponding bit.
Return the level when a full-mask state is popped; -1 if the queue empties.
a.t: O(m·n·2^L·(energy+1)) states, each expanded in O(1) — bounded by ~20M operations for the given limits
a.sp: O(m·n·2^L·(energy+1)) for the visited set and queue

w: Use the full-state BFS in an interview — it is the canonical solution and easy to justify. Pitfalls: forgetting that energy 0 blocks movement even onto non-'R' cells, forgetting that 'R' resets unconditionally (even from full energy), and off-by-one on when the mask becomes complete (check on pop, or on generation). Follow-ups: what if litter count grows past 20 (need different techniques, e.g., BFS between landmarks + TSP-style DP), or if energy costs varied (switch to Dijkstra).
